text:
maria: Quick note — noticed recurring 429 spikes on weekends hitting our paging thresholds. Pattern: short (1-3m) bursts from a handful of orgs that use webhook fanout. Pages wake folks up but most incidents auto-resolve. Proposal: change alerting to reduce noise while keeping customer visibility. Ideas below, want quick feedback before I open a PR.

maria: Proposal TL;DR:
- switch primary 429 alert from instantaneous >X to a 5m rolling window with z-score detection
- only page SRE if >5% of org's keys exceed threshold OR if >N requests/sec for entire org for 5m
- route lower-severity signals to CS queue (cs@) so CSMs can proactively contact customers
- add a dashboard heatmap for top 20 orgs by 429-rate and a short-lived spike panel

tim: +1 on rolling window. Also add a suppression window for known maintenance intervals (we already have a label for scheduled-maintenance). Short bursts are fine if they don't exceed error budget for the org.

joy: For the detection side, here's a candidate PromQL (replace metric names as needed):
```
# per-org 5m rolling 429 rate
sum(rate(http_status{code="429"}[5m])) by (org)
# normalized per-1000 requests
(sum(rate(http_status{code="429"}[5m])) by (org)) / (sum(rate(http_total_requests[5m])) by (org)) * 1000
# z-score-ish approach (quick): compare current 5m against 6h moving average
current = sum(rate(http_status{code="429"}[5m])) by (org)
baseline = increase(http_status{code="429"}[6h]) / 21600
```
We should avoid paging for orgs where baseline is already high unless absolute rate crosses X.

olivia: Dashboard notes — add a heatmap with orgs on y-axis and 5m 429-rate buckets on x. Also add a small table: top 10 affected keys + recent deploy/git commit to help triage. We should surface whether the traffic pattern is bursty (high p95 token use) vs sustained.

cs_lead: From CS POV: If pages are lowered, we still need timely customer-facing visibility. Suggest a routed Slack notification to #cs-alerts with org, rate, sample request IDs, and a recommended message template for CSMs. Also require an "impact" field in the alert so CSM can prioritize (impact = %keys affected OR rate pct).

maria: Good call. I can add an action that posts to #cs-alerts with a JSON payload (org, 429_rate, keys_impacted, sample_log_links). Example action: `curl -X POST https://hooks.slack.com/services/... -d '{"text":"Org acme-inc: 429 spike — 12 keys affected (4.1% of keys) — p95 latency up 30%"}'`

tim: We'll also need a short runbook snippet to avoid repeated re-page loops. Suggestion:
1) Check dashboard heatmap + top keys panel
2) If >5% keys affected -> escalate to oncall and CS
3) If <5% and spikes <3m -> mark as "fanout burst" and watch for repeat in 30m
4) If repeat within an hour, escalate

maria: I'll add that to the runbook and link to the dashboard.

sre-bot: Alert fired: 1767901500 - 429_spike_rule - org:acme-inc - 5m_rate: 42/s - keys_impacted: 14 (6.3%) - severity: page

cs_lead: Saw the bot message. Could we include a small sample curl for customers (CS template) so CSMs can paste it and ask for webhook configs? Also include whether the org is on dedicated vs hosted routing.

olivia: I'll update the dashboard to include routing tier column. Also adding a small histogram of inter-arrival times to help identify whether it's a misbehaving client or genuine traffic.

maria: Plan of action: (1) I'll open a PR to change the alerting rule to 5m rolling + org impact gating, (2) olivia will update the dashboard with heatmap + routing tier, (3) tim will add suppression for scheduled-maintenance and dedupe logic, (4) cs_lead will prepare CS Slack template and escalation guidance. We'll ship in a small rollout: test on staging next 48h, then 10% rule rollout, then global.

maria: If no objections by EOD I'll start the PR and tag owners. Thanks! :pray:
